exampleText: My mom starts chemo next week and I'm scared. Please pray for her and for me.

devotional.opening: Thank you for trusting this moment with prayer. You are not alone in what you are carrying.

saints.name: St. Dymphna
saints.story: By tradition an Irish princess who fled to Belgium to escape her father's abuse and was martyred there. In the town of Geel, devotion to her grew into a centuries-old tradition of families welcoming people with mental illness into their homes.
saints.why: St. Dymphna is a patron of mental health and anxiety and depression. By tradition an Irish princess who fled to Belgium to escape her father's abuse and was martyred there.

saints.name: St. Raphael the Archangel
saints.region: Named in the Book of Tobit
saints.story: His name means "God heals." In the Book of Tobit he travels in disguise with young Tobias, protects him on the road, helps him find his wife Sarah, and brings healing to Tobias's blind father.
saints.why: St. Raphael the Archangel is a patron of healing and travelers. His name means "God heals." In the Book of Tobit he travels in disguise with young Tobias, protects him on the road, helps him find his wife Sarah, and brings healing to Tobias's blind father..

saints.name: St. Jude Thaddeus
saints.story: One of the Twelve Apostles. By tradition he preached the Gospel and was martyred. Because his name resembled Judas, he was long overlooked — and so the faithful came to turn to him when they felt they had nowhere else to go.
saints.why: St. Jude Thaddeus is a patron of desperate situations and lost causes. One of the Twelve Apostles.

prayer.title: A prayer for today
prayer.body:
Loving God, You know what is on my heart before I can find the words. I come to You just as I am today.

I place before You my family, with all its wounds and love, and my body and its healing, and what I am afraid of. Where I am weary, be my rest. Where I am afraid, be my courage. Where I cannot see the way, be my light.

St. Dymphna and St. Raphael the Archangel, you knew struggle and grace in your own lives — pray for me, that I may trust that nothing is wasted in God's hands.

Stay close today, Lord. Let me feel that I am held, and let me hold others with the same tenderness.

scripture.text: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul. Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me.
scripture.connection: A word to rest in today, slowly, more than once.

scripture.text: Don't be afraid, for I am with you. Don't be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
scripture.connection: A word to rest in today, slowly, more than once.

devotions.title: Prayer to St. Michael the Archangel
devotions.text: St. Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle. Be our protection against the wickedness and snares of the devil. May God rebuke him, we humbly pray; and do thou, O Prince of the heavenly host, by the power of God, cast into hell Satan and all the evil spirits who prowl about the world seeking the ruin of souls. Amen.
devotions.suggestion: Pray it slowly, perhaps once in the morning and once at night.

devotions.title: The Sorrowful Mysteries
devotions.suggestion: If a whole Rosary feels like too much today, one decade is a beautiful prayer.

devotions.title: The Divine Mercy Chaplet
devotions.description: Prayed on ordinary rosary beads, traditionally at 3 p.m., the hour of mercy. On each bead: "For the sake of His sorrowful Passion, have mercy on us and on the whole world." It takes about seven minutes.
devotions.suggestion: Pray it slowly, perhaps once in the morning and once at night.

devotional.reflection: Courage is not the absence of fear. It is one small yes, said while trembling.
